Introduction

This is the method that I use to launch Gamecube and Wii games using the Dolphin emulator and Steam. This is extremely convenient as it can all be done with a controller using Steam Big-Picture mode. I'm not claiming that this is the only method that can be used (it definitely isn't), but it is what I use and would recommend to other people. I also can't say that I originally came up with this method, but it is a combination of what I've seen other people do and what I personally do.

1. Get the emulator

Download the latest developer version of Dolphin here:

https://dolphin-emu.org/download/

They're said to be less stable than the latest "stable" release (4.0.2), however from my experience they actually perform a lot better than the "stable" versions. If for some reason you're having trouble with developer builds, try the latest stable release instead.

2. Obtain your ISO image(s)

I'm not going to link directly to any "pirated" content, but you can generally get Gamecube ISOs from various emulation sites (Emuparadise is great). Wii ISOs/WBFSs aren't as easy to get. You'll either have to get these using a soft-modded Wii or use torrents, but I wouldn't recommend torrents since they're illegal.

3. Set up the emulator

Dolphin is fairly easy to use, so you won't have to tinker with much to get it to work with your system. I'm not going to cover how to configure everything, since there's plenty of tutorials for that. Just do the typical stuff, like making sure that dual-core is enabled, doing your various enhancements, configuring your controller(s), etc, etc. What is critical to do is to make sure that you're using the Direct3D backend! Trying to launch games with Steam using the OpenGL backend will cause the game to glitch very, very badly! This is due to the Steam overlay and Steam Big-Picture Mode using OpenGL, which will cause them to hijack some OpenGL functions from Dolphin and cause the emulator to glitch out.

4. Launch Steam

Once you have everything in Dolphin setup, go ahead and launch steam.

5. Add Dolphin as a Non-Steam Game

Make sure you're under the library tab in Steam, and click on "Add a Game...", then "Add a Non-Steam Game". Click on "Browse..." and find the directory of where you installed Dolphin (in my case, the path is "C:\Emulation\Gamecube and Wii\Dolphin\Dolphin.exe"). Then click on "Add Selected Programs".

6. Set the launch options for the game that you want to add

If you click on the shortcut that you just made, only Dolphin will launch. In order to launch the game itself, find the shortcut that you just made for Dolphin, right click on it and click "Properties". Go down to the "Target" box, and type in:

"(Path of where you installed Dolphin)" /e "(Path of where the game you want to launch is)" /b

Don't include the parentheses, but make sure you have the quotation marks. For example, if I wanted to add Super Smash Bros Melee, in my case it would look like:

"C:\Emulation\Gamecube and Wii\Dolphin\Dolphin.exe" /e "C:\Emulation\Gamecube and Wii\ISOs\Super Smash Bros. Melee.iso" /b

Once you have your Target made, rename the shortcut (first box under "properties", it should just be Dolphin right now) to whatever the name of the game is that you added. (This isn't necessary, although I'd strongly recommend it for organizational purposes.) Close the "Properties" window once you're finished.

7. Test out the shortcut

Try launching the game to see if it actually works or not. If it works, then you can go to the next step. If it fails or just launches Dolphin, go back and make sure that you put the right info under "Target" in "Properties". A mistake I've made before is not having the right extension for the image (it isn't always .iso, it could also be .gcm or .wbfs). Missing quotation marks can also cause it it to fail.

8. Set a combination on your controller that will exit the emulator (Optional)

This can be convenient if you just want to do everything from your controller, BUT you could always accidentally press the combination in the middle of a game and lose your progress. This has never happened to me, but you might not want to take the risk of this potentially happening.

Anyways, if you want to do this, use some controller remapping program to remap "Alt" and "F4" to your controller. Personally, I use an Xbox 360 controller, so I used Xpadder and remapped "Alt" to the Left Bumper and "F4" to the "Back" button, since these are two of the only buttons that I'm not using for Dolphin.

9. Set custom images for your added games (Also optional)

Once you have your games added, you can add some custom images to the games you added. This isn't necessary, but it does look a lot better in your Steam library (in Big-Picture Mode at least). The images you want to add should be 460x215. It's kind of a pain to find images on Google so I've included an imgur link for images for several games. None of these are my original creation; I've just found them through a ridiculous amount of searching.

http://imgur.com/a/x372J

You can set custom images by going to your library, clicking on the third option up by "View" in the upper right of Steam (it should be the option with four little boxes). Find the game that you want to add a custom image to, right click it, select "Set Custom Image...", click "Browse..." and select the image that you want to add. Close out of the window and repeat for the rest of the games you added.

That's it!
